Rashi on Sotah 24b:1:1.english: Shaamum (stupefaction) - Afflicted with bewilderment of the heart.

Rashi on Sotah 24b:1:2.hebrew: האי תחת אישה - בתראה, האמור בסוף הפרשה: "זאת תורת הקנאות" וגו':
Rashi on Sotah 24b:1:2.english: This "under her husband" - The latter one, which is stated at the end of the passage: "This is the law of jealousies," etc.

Rashi on Sotah 24b:1:3.hebrew: להקיש אשה לאיש - ברייתא היא בשילהי פרקין, והתם מפרש למאי הלכתא:
Rashi on Sotah 24b:1:3.english: To compare a woman to a man - It is a baraita near the end of this chapter, and there it explains for what halakhic purpose [this comparison is made].

Rashi on Sotah 24b:2:1.english: These verses - which exclude a betrothed woman:

Rashi on Sotah 24b:2:2.hebrew: מבלעדי אישך - משמע שבעלה נתן בה את שכבתו קודם לסתירה זו:
Rashi on Sotah 24b:2:2.english: Besides your husband - This implies that her husband had already given his seminal emission into her before this seclusion.

Rashi on Sotah 24b:3:1.hebrew: משכחת לה - דאיצטריך למעוטי ארוסה מקרא אחרינא, ולא ממעטא מהתם:
Rashi on Sotah 24b:3:1.english: You can find it - [A case] where it is necessary to exclude a betrothed woman from another verse, and it is not excluded from there.

Rashi on Sotah 24b:3:2.hebrew: כגון שבא עליה ארוס בבית אביה - בזנות:
Rashi on Sotah 24b:3:2.english: For example, where her betrothed had relations with her in her father's house - Through licentiousness.

Rashi on Sotah 24b:4:1.english: In the house of her father-in-law - After his brother died.

Rashi on Sotah 24b:4:2.hebrew: שומרת יבם קרית לה - דקאמרת דלא תשתה, הא אשתו מעלייתא היא בביאת זנות:
Rashi on Sotah 24b:4:2.english: Do you call her a "woman awaiting her yavam"? - [You call her this] because you say that she does not drink [the bitter waters]; but behold, she is his full-fledged wife through the act of licentious intercourse.

Rashi on Sotah 24b:4:3.hebrew: דהא אמר רב - ביבמות קנה לכל. דתנן: הבא על יבמתו, בין בשוגג בין במזיד — דהיינו בזנות — קנה. ואמר רב: קנה דקתני מתני' — קנה לכל: אם כהן הוא, מאכילה בתרומה, ויורשה, ומיטמא לה, ומשקה, ופוטרה בגט בלא חליצה:
Rashi on Sotah 24b:4:3.english: For Rav said - In the case of yevamot, he has acquired her for all purposes. For we learned in a Mishnah: One who has relations with his yevamah, whether unintentionally or intentionally — that is, in a licentious manner — has acquired her. And Rav said: [The word] "acquired" that the Mishnah teaches means he has acquired her for all purposes: if he is a kohen, he may feed her terumah, and he inherits her, and he may become ritually impure for her, and he gives her the bitter waters to drink, and he releases her with a bill of divorce without chalitzah.

Rashi on Sotah 24b:5:1.hebrew: כשמואל - הא דאתא קרא למעוטי כשמואל, דאמר: לא קנה אלא לדברים האמורים בפרשת יבמה — לקום על שם אחיו בנחלתו, ולפוטרה בגט. דהא דקני לה יבם בביאה כל דהו, "מיבמה יבא עליה" נפקא לן, דלא כתיב "יבמה יקחנה לו לאשה" אלא "יבא עליה ולקחה לו לאשה", ואשמעינן דביאתו עליה הן הן ליקוחי האישות שלו. הלכך למידי דאיתמר בהך פרשתא, רבינהו קרא — נישואין הללו; אבל למידי אחרינא לאו נישואין נינהו. ומה אמור בפרשה? פטור חליצה ע"י יבום, ו"יקום על שם אחיו" — שיורש את נכסי אחיו, ואין אחיו חולקין עמו:
Rashi on Sotah 24b:5:1.english: Like Shmuel - The verse comes to exclude [a case] according to Shmuel, who said: He acquired her only for the matters stated in the passage of the yevama — to establish [a child] upon his brother's name in his inheritance, and to release her with a bill of divorce. For [the ruling] that the yavam acquires her through any act of intercourse, we derive from "her yavam shall come upon her," for it does not write "her yavam shall take her as a wife," but rather "he shall come upon her and take her to himself as a wife." And it teaches us that his intercourse with her is itself his marriage-taking. Therefore, for whatever is stated in this passage, the verse included this marriage; but for anything else, it is not marriage. And what is stated in the passage? The exemption from chalitza through yibbum, and "he shall arise upon the name of his brother" — that he inherits his brother's property, and his brothers do not share it with him.

Rashi on Sotah 24b:6:1.hebrew: לימא רב - דאמר קנה לכל, כרבי יאשיה, דאמר שומרת יבם שותה, ואוקימנא בבא עליה:
Rashi on Sotah 24b:6:1.english: Shall we say that Rav - who said that [the yavam] acquired [her] for all [purposes], is in accordance with Rabbi Yoshiyah, who said that a woman awaiting her yavam [must] drink [the bitter waters], and we established [this as referring to a case where the yavam] had relations with her:

Rashi on Sotah 24b:6:2.hebrew: אנא דאמרי אפילו כרבי יונתן כו' - וכל שכן כרבי יאשיה. והא דאיצטריך לרבי יאשיה לרבויי מ"איש איש", לאו דוקא, אלא אסמכתא בעלמא, ועיקר קרא לאשת חרש ושוטה:
Rashi on Sotah 24b:6:2.english: I say that even [it is] like Rabbi Yonatan, etc. - And all the more so like Rabbi Yoshiyah. And as for the fact that Rabbi Yoshiyah needed to include [this] from "ish ish" ("any man"), it is not exact; rather, it is merely an asmakhta (a textual support), and the main [purpose of the] verse is for the wife of a deaf-mute or an imbecile.

Tosafot on Sotah 24b:1:1.hebrew: ורבי יונתן האי איש איש מאי עביד ליה וכו' - תימה: האי ריבוי לרבי יאשיה מנליה, והיקישא דאיש לאשה לר' יונתן מנא ליה? וכי אית לן למימר דפליגי בהא נמי, דר' יאשיה לית ליה דאשת חרש שותה, ור' יונתן לית ליה דסומא אינה שותה:
Tosafot on Sotah 24b:1:1.english: "And Rabbi Yonatan, this 'ish ish' (a man, a man) — what does he do with it?" etc. - This is puzzling: From where does Rabbi Yoshiyah derive this extension, and from where does Rabbi Yonatan derive the analogy of 'ish' to 'ishah' (man to woman)? Must we say that they disagree about this as well — that Rabbi Yoshiyah does not hold that [the wife of] a deaf man drinks, and Rabbi Yonatan does not hold that [the wife of] a blind man does not drink?

Tosafot on Sotah 24b:4:1.hebrew: דהאמר רב קנה לכל - הני לישני דפליגי בהבא על יבמתו (יבמות דף נח.): בשומרת יבם שנפלה מן הנשואין או מן האירוסין, לא שייכא דוקא אלא לענין תרומה, משום דכבר אכלה; אבל לענין להשקותה וליורשה ולטמא לה — לא:
Tosafot on Sotah 24b:4:1.english: For Rav said: He acquired her for all [purposes] - These versions [of Rav's statement], which disagree about one who has relations with his yevamah (Yevamot 58a): With regard to a *shomeret yavam* [a woman awaiting levirate marriage] who fell to the yavam from marriage or from betrothal, [Rav's ruling] applies only with respect to *terumah*, because she had already eaten it; but with respect to making her drink [the *sotah* waters], inheriting her, and becoming ritually impure for her — [he did] not [acquire her].

Tosafot on Sotah 24b:5:1.hebrew: כשמואל דאמר לא קנה אלא לדברים כו' - תימה: כיון דקנה מיהת לדברים האמורים בפרשה, לפוטרה בגט — דכיון שבא עליה הרי היא כאשתו לאותן דברים — א"כ מ"ט דרבי יונתן דאלימא ליה ארוסה משומרת יבם? אי משום דארוסה קידושין דידיה, שומרת יבם נמי ביאה דידיה היא, ונחנקה על ידו! וכ"ש דתקשה לרב דאמר "אנא דאמינא אפילו לרבי יונתן". ותו, מאי דוחקיה למימר כשמואל? והא מסיק דאפילו רב הוה אתי מלתייהו אליביה! ולענין השקאה קפיד רחמנא דבעינן ביאה לשם אישות. וביבמות בפרק הבא על יבמתו (יבמות דף נח.) מוקי לה נמי הא דתנן [אמן שלא שטיתי ארוסה ונשואה] "שומרת יבם וכנוסה", כגון דבא עליה יבם בבית אחיו וכו' כי הכא. ומקשה: מידי הוא טעמא אלא לרב? האמר רב: קנה לכל! ולא מתרץ גבי השקאה: גזירת הכתוב דבעינן ביאה לשם אישות:
Tosafot on Sotah 24b:5:1.english: Like Shmuel, who said: He acquired her only for the matters stated in the passage, etc. - This is difficult: Since he has, at any rate, acquired her for the matters stated in the passage, to release her with a get — for since he had relations with her, she is like his wife for those matters — then what is the reason of Rabbi Yonatan, to whom an betrothed woman seems stronger than a woman awaiting yibum? If it is because betrothal is his own act of marriage, then a woman awaiting yibum, too, has relations that are his own, and she is [liable to be] strangled through him! All the more so should this be difficult for Rav, who said, "I said [my ruling] even according to Rabbi Yonatan." And furthermore, what forces him to say [that it is] like Shmuel? Surely the Gemara concludes that even Rav's words work out according to him! And as for the drinking [of the bitter waters], the Merciful One is particular that we require relations for the sake of marriage. And in Yevamot, in the chapter "One who has relations with his yevamah" (Yevamot 58a), [the Gemara] also establishes the Mishnah's statement ["Amen — that I have not strayed, whether betrothed or married"] as referring to "a woman awaiting yibum, and one who has been taken in marriage," where the yavam had relations with her in his brother's house, etc., as here. And it asks: Is that a reason [at all], except according to Rav? Didn't Rav say that he acquired her for everything! And it does not answer, with regard to the drinking, that it is a decree of the verse that we require relations for the sake of marriage.

Tosafot on Sotah 24b:6:1.hebrew: בספרים גרס: "אי הכי, לימא רב דאמר כרבי יאשיה", ולא א"ש "אי הכי". ובפרש"י לא גרס "אי הכי", והוא לא שבש הגירסא אלא בסתם. פי': "לימא רב דאמר" וכו'. ושמא בספרו לא היה כתוב "אי הכי":
Tosafot on Sotah 24b:6:1.english: In the books [i.e., manuscripts or texts] the reading is: "If so, shall we say that Rav, who said [his ruling] like Rabbi Yoshiyah..." — but the phrase "if so" does not fit well. And in Rashi's commentary he does not read "if so," and he did not corrupt the reading, but [wrote] only in a general way. He explains: "Shall we say that Rav, who said," etc. And perhaps in his copy the words "if so" were not written:

Tosafot on Sotah 24b:6:2.hebrew: אמר לך אנא דאמרי אפי' לרבי יונתן - נראה דהכי פירושו: לא מיבעיא לרבי יאשיה דמרבה שומרת יבם דאמינא כוותיה, והאי דאיצטריך לרבויי משום דכתיב הכא "תחת אישך" דמשמע שבא עליה לשם אישות וכו', לא צריכא למימר דקרא אסמכתא בעלמא הוא, כמו שפירש רש"י. ואף מה שפירש לשמואל, ההיא דאיצטריך רבי יונתן למעוטי שומרת יבם — אסמכתא בעלמא הוא. תימה: נהי דלאו אשתו היא, אי לאו מעטיה קרא מהיכא תיתי דבעינן אשתו טפי לענין השקאה מלענין קינוי? אי משום דכתיב "והביא האיש את אשתו" (אלא) ה"נ גבי קינוי כתיב "וקינא את אשתו". ירושלמי: ארוסה לא שותה? "וישקנה" — גזירת הכתוב הוא. "והביא האיש את אשתו" ולא יקנא לה? התורה אמרה "וקינא את אשתו", "וקינא את אשתו" — אפי' מקצת אשתו. ר' יודן בעי: כמה דתימר תמן "וקינא את אשתו", "וקינא את אשתו" — אפילו מקצת אשתו; דכוותה "תחת אישך", "תחת אישך" — אפי' מקצת אישך. היך עבידה? קינא לה ועודה ארוסה, וכנסה ונסתרה — משקה אותה על קינויו. קינא לה עודה שומרת יבם, וכנסה ונסתרה — משקה אותה על קינויו. קינא לה ועודה ארוסה, וכנסה ונסתרה וידע בה — תצא בכתובתה, ואם לאו — תצא שלא בכתובתה. (קינא לה ועודה שומרת יבם, וכנסה ונסתרה וידע בה — תצא בכתובתה, ואם לאו — תצא שלא בכתובתה) לא קינא לה בעלה ומת ונפלה לפני היבם, וקינא לה ולא הספיק לכונסה עד שמת ונפלה לפני אחיו — אינו משקה אותה, שלא נפלה לו אלא מחמת אחיו הראשון. אבל אם קינא לה היבם וכנסה ומת ונפלה לפני היבם וכנסה ונסתרה — משקה אותה על קינויו:
Tosafot on Sotah 24b:6:2.english: "He can say to you: I say [this] even according to Rabbi Yonatan" - It appears that its explanation is as follows: It is not necessary [to say this] according to Rabbi Yoshiyah, who includes a *shomeret yavam* (a woman awaiting levirate marriage), for I would say it according to him; and [as for] the fact that it was necessary to include her, because it is written here "under your husband," which implies that he had relations with her for the sake of marriage, etc. — it was unnecessary to say [this], since the verse is merely a scriptural support (*asmakhta*), as Rashi explained. And even what [Rashi] explained according to Shmuel — that [the verse] that Rabbi Yonatan needed in order to exclude a *shomeret yavam* is merely an *asmakhta* — is puzzling: Granted that she is not his wife, had the verse not excluded her, from where would we have derived that we require [that she be] his wife more for the matter of giving [the waters] to drink than for the matter of warning? If [you say it is] because it is written, "and the man shall bring his wife" (but) — so too with regard to warning it is written, "and he shall warn his wife." The Yerushalmi [says]: A betrothed woman does not drink? "And he shall make her drink" — it is a decree of Scripture. "And the man shall bring his wife" — and shall he not warn her? The Torah said, "and he shall warn his wife"; "and he shall warn his wife" — even part of his wife. Rabbi Yudan asked: Just as you say there, "and he shall warn his wife," "and he shall warn his wife" — even part of his wife; likewise here, "under your husband," "under your husband" — even part of your husband. How does this work? If he warned her while she was still betrothed, and then married her and she secluded herself [with the man], he makes her drink on account of his warning. If he warned her while she was still a *shomeret yavam*, and then married her and she secluded herself, he makes her drink on account of his warning. If he warned her while she was still betrothed, and then married her and she secluded herself and he knew of it (i.e., that she had been defiled), she leaves with her *ketubah*, and if not, she leaves without her *ketubah*. (If he warned her while she was still a *shomeret yavam*, and then married her and she secluded herself and he knew of it, she leaves with her *ketubah*, and if not, she leaves without her *ketubah*.) If her husband had not warned her and died, and she fell to the yavam; or he warned her and did not manage to marry her before he died, and she fell to his brother — he does not make her drink, because she fell to him only by virtue of his first brother. But if the yavam warned her and married her, and [then] died, and she fell to the [other] yavam, and he married her and she secluded herself — he makes her drink on account of his warning.
